newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius bourse awaits privatisation listings.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius bourse awaits privatisation listings.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM) is expecting fresh listings from government privatisation of a number of state assets, said Richard Morin, the bourse's chief executive.

He said the Indian Ocean island was looking forward to several new share issues over the next two years, flowing from government plans to sell stakes in key holdings and as firms moved to SEM from its predecessor, the over-the-counter market.
"There's considerable potential for initial public offerings as part of government's privatisation programme. Everyone is talking about Mauritius Telecom," Morin told Reuters in an interview.
Although labour unions have strongly opposed the restructuring of the telecommunications firm, the process was likely to carry on although the initial deadline of June 30 would not be met, he said.
"Personally I would see no reason not to (privatise Mauritius Telecom) in the course of 1997 or 1998," Morin said.
Another potential candidate for privatisation was Sicom, the state insurance company, he said.
Two state concerns, Mauritius Commercial Bank and the State Bank of Mauritius, have already been partially privatised and listed on SEM.
"There, too, we are awaiting secondary offerings," Morin said.

The banks are by far the two biggest firms by market capitalisation on the bourse, which was set up in 1989 and currently sports 45 listed firms across seven industry sectors. Government still holds controlling interests in both banks.

New listings on SEM, which at the end of February had a total market capitalisation of 34.6 billion rupees, have grown at an average rate of over five a year, mostly as companies from the OTC market offered their shares publicly.

Morin said there were still a few OTC-listed firms which were good candidates for the official SEM list. Floreal Knitwear, a Mauritian textile firm which also has operations in Madagascar, was a likely mover.
"We expect to see them on the official list in the next few months," he said.
Major projects earmarked for SEM during 1997 and 1998 include the automation of stock trading, which is currently done by open-outcry, and which should help improve liquidity.

SEM statistics show average turnover per session last year at 10.82 million rupees, which leaves the ratio of turnover to market capitalisation of the key SEMDEX index at only five percent -- well below that of other emerging markets. Morin said the bourse was also in the process of adopting a new securities and exchange act to improve investor protection whilst also reducing regulatory intervention.
SEM in January launched a fully computerised and independent central depositary and settlement firm.
